title: Staged-gate admin access intake and request classifier
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Summary: Build a staged-gate intake flow and automated classifier for admin & access requests (RBAC/SSO/SCIM/org policy). Goal is to reduce mean time to resolution for high-priority enterprise access changes, reduce manual triage load, and provide an auditable escalation path.

Scope:
- Inbound channels: support portal, account manager intake form, partner SSO onboarding sheet.
- Classifier: lightweight rules + supervised model to tag requests by type (RBAC change, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning, org-policy exception) and assign an initial priority and guardrail checklist.
- Staged gates: Auto-ack -> Auto-approve (low-risk) / Human-review (mid/high-risk) -> Security approval -> Completed.
- Integration points: Console request API, Audit log service, SLA dashboard, Alerts to on-call, GitHub PRs for policy changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Classifier accuracy: >= 85% precision on RBAC vs SSO labels in pilot dataset.
- Reduction in manual triage volume by 40% for supported channels after rollout.
- All escalations produce a traceable audit event with decision reason and linking to related PRs or Confluence docs.
- TTL enforcement: requests without human review escalate automatically after 48 hours for high priority.

Success metrics:
- Median time from request creation to resolution for high-impact requests falls below 72 hours.
- Number of requests misclassified leading to incorrect approvals <= 2% in first 90 days.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Initial classifier will prioritize precision over recall to avoid granting access incorrectly.
- We'll implement rules for known edge cases (e.g., cross-org role inheritance) before full model rollout.
- SCIM/SSO onboarding requires idP metadata validation step; that adds latency but is necessary for security.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Leah Chen (owner), Marco Liu (assignee)
- Eng: Serving-runtime & Console teams
- Security & Compliance: review & approval gate
- Solutions/Customer Success: pilot customers and intake form design

Open questions:
- Where does the canonical audit record live for multi-step approvals? (Console will own + forward to central audit)
- Do we allow delegated approvals for certain partner tiers? (proposal: yes, with scoped tokens)

2026-03-06 - Engineering update (Marco Liu): ENG-4021 created for data export and feature engineering. Preliminary dataset has ~2.1k labeled requests across channels. Missing consistent 'customer_tier' field — Solutions will add to intake form. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/789

2026-03-08 - Security feedback (Jamal Ortiz): Must require idp_entity_id and SAML metadata checksum before any auto-approve. Added security checkpoint to Staged Gate. Action: add validation step and update SLA expectations.

2026-03-09 - Design review (Priya Sharma): New intake form mockups created to capture minimum SCIM/SSO fields and 'requested-roles' selector to improve classifier signal. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENT/Staged-Gate+Intake+UX

2026-03-10 - Trade-off note: We debated immediate auto-approval for 'read-only' RBAC requests for lower tiers. Decided to gate auto-approve to customer tier + requested scope. Manual override allowed by Security with audit reason.

2026-03-11 - Engineering note: Pilot classifier (rule+logistic reg) achieves 88% precision at 72% recall on held-out set for RBAC vs SSO labels. Next: integrate into intake service with a debug flag to record predictions but not act (canary).
2026-03-12 - Ops: Added escalation path doc; high-priority requests now create incidents with paging rules. Incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Admin+Intake+Escalation

2026-03-13 - PM decision: Move forward with beta rollout to 3 enterprise customers for early feedback. Create pilot playbook and schedule weekly syncs with CS. Next milestone: ENG to deliver feature branch for canary (due 2026-03-20).
